analysis:
This PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The visible head-side changes are the scheduler configuration table (lines 1087-1090) and a new "Prompt geometry" section (lines 1102-1159). It documents Gemma 4 moving to a 2048-token prefill chunk and 4096-token step, a 512-token ceiling for bidirectional media chunks, and the per-family exceptions. The changed ranges also list 2041-2060, which is outside the supplied units, so I did not review it.

The documentation describes no new endpoints, authentication, key handling or attestation changes. The cache description does not change TTL, HMAC lookup names, salt scoping or the encryption design in T-041. It says the geometry override keys enter the complete-checkpoint numerics fingerprint (`PrefixCachePolicy.completeCheckpointIdentity`), so cache identity is unchanged in kind. It also says explicit overrides disqualify reviewed serving and deadline profiles.

The prose also asserts, with no code visible here to confirm it, that the paged pool's `maxPrefillChunk` and the windowed-ring KV charges stay unchanged. It states that decode-token p99 gaps grow two to three times. That is a latency/availability tradeoff for Gemma 4 rows sharing a step, not a confidentiality or integrity regression.

The real security risk is in the underlying code change (EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift `prefillGeometry` and the memory floors). That code is outside the supplied units and was not reviewed. Whether the memory admission floors still hold at 2048/4096 is relevant to T-010/T-029 availability. The doc cites 2026-10-21 measurements, but I could not verify them.

No findings are raised. Integration should check, if the code is in scope, that the wide-chunk path respects KV budget admission and that media requests keep the 512 ceiling.
